propositions.text: The appellant is a Tunisian citizen appealing the RPD decision rejecting his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The appellant, XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Tunisia, is appealing against the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD), which rejected his claim for refugee protection

propositions.text: The RPD found the appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: which rejected his claim for refugee protection by finding that he is neither a "Convention refugee" nor a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The appellant, a Tunisian citizen, appeals the RPD decision rejecting his refugee claim as neither a Convention refugee nor person in need of protection.

propositions.text: Appellant's counsel asks RAD to allow appeal, set aside RPD decision, find protection need or refer for re-determination by different member.
propositions.quote: counsel for the appellant is asking the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to allow the appeal, set aside the RPD determination, determine that the appellant is a person in need of protection or refer the matter to the RPD for re-determination

paragraphs.summary: Appellant's counsel asks RAD to allow appeal, set aside RPD decision, find protection need or refer for re-determination by different member.

propositions.text: Memorandum claims evidence was presented per IRPA 110(4) but no new evidence or submission included.
propositions.quote: The memorandum indicates that [translation] "evidence was presented in accordance with the requirements of subsection 110(4) of the IRPA for this appeal," yet no new evidence or submission was included with the appellant's record.

propositions.text: No new evidence was submitted in support of this appeal.
propositions.quote: In this context, I find that no new evidence was submitted in support of this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: Memorandum claims evidence was presented but no new evidence included; court finds no new evidence submitted for appeal.

propositions.text: Appellant requests a hearing and interpreter services for spouse's testimony.
propositions.quote: In the memorandum, the appellant is requesting that a hearing be held and requires the services of an interpreter so that his spouse can testify.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant requests a hearing and interpreter services for spouse's testimony.

propositions.text: RAD confirms RPD's determination that appellant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection under IRPA.
propositions.quote: the RAD confirms the determination of the RPD, namely, that XXXX XXXX is neither a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA nor a "person in need of protection" under section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: RAD confirms RPD's determination that appellant is neither Convention refugee nor person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The appeal is dismissed.

propositions.text: Claimant is Tunisian Muslim who came to Canada in 2014 and claimed refugee protection in 2015 due to fear of persecution for marrying a Catholic woman and attending church.
propositions.quote: The refugee protection claimant is a citizen of Tunisia and a Muslim. He came to Canada as a visitor on XXXX XXXX, 2014. He made a refugee protection claim on May 4, 2015. He alleges a well-founded fear of persecution and a risk to his life by reason of his marriage to a Catholic woman in XXXX 2015 and his attending Catholic churches.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant is Tunisian Muslim who fears persecution for marrying a Catholic woman and attending church, claimed refugee protection in 2015.

propositions.text: In BOC Form, claimant alleges dating a Catholic woman and agreeing to convert to Christianity to marry her; family informed.
propositions.quote: In his Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form), he alleges that he began dating an XXXX woman of the Catholic faith. He agreed to convert to Christianity in order to marry his wife. The claimant's parents were informed of his marriage and that he was going to church in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant alleges dating Catholic woman, agreed to convert to Christianity to marry, and family was informed.

propositions.text: Claimant's family considers him a shame; alleges death penalty in Tunisia for changing religion.
propositions.quote: His family in Tunisia considers him a shame on the family. He alleges that, in Tunisia, death awaits anyone who changes religion.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's family considers him shame; alleges death penalty in Tunisia for changing religion.

propositions.text: RPD rejected claim, found claimant not credible and testimony untrustworthy on central claim elements.
propositions.quote: On July 27, 2015, the RPD rejected the refugee protection claim, finding that [translation] "the claimant was not credible and his testimony was not trustworthy with regard to the central elements of the claim."

propositions.text: RPD noted omissions, inconsistencies, implausibilities; believed claimant did not convert or intend to convert to Catholicism.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted several omissions in the BOC Form, and inconsistencies and implausibilities in the evidence. In short, the RPD [translation] "believes that the claimant did not convert to Catholicism and did not demonstrate that he intended to do so."

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from lack of corroboration on willingness to convert.
propositions.quote: the panel draws a negative inference from the claimant's lack of effort to corroborate his testimony on his willingness to convert to Catholicism.

paragraphs.summary: RPD rejected claim as not credible, noting omissions, inconsistencies, and lack of corroboration on conversion intent.

propositions.text: RPD found no prohibition on Muslim-Christian marriage and no systematic persecution of such couples in Tunisia.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that the documentary evidence indicates that there is nothing prohibiting Muslims from marrying non-Muslims, and that there are many mixed couples in Tunisia. According to the RPD, the evidence does not allow for the conclusion that Muslims married to Christians are systematically persecuted in Tunisia.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found no prohibition or systematic persecution of Muslim-Christian marriages in Tunisia.

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD erred by rejecting refugee protection claim.
propositions.quote: The appellant submits that the RPD erred by rejecting his refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant submits RPD erred in rejecting refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Appellant relies on Maldonado that sworn testimony is presumed true unless valid reason to doubt.
propositions.quote: The appellant is relying on Maldonado and submits that sworn testimony is presumed to be true, unless there is a valid reason to doubt its truthfulness.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant relies on Maldonado that sworn testimony is presumed true unless valid reason to doubt.

propositions.text: Appellant cites Giron advising caution on adverse findings from implausibilities due to cultural differences.
propositions.quote: He also cited the Federal Court of Appeal decision in Giron, which advises caution when making adverse findings based on implausibilities because refugee protection claimants come from diverse cultures and "actions which might appear implausible if judged by Canadian standards might be plausible when considered within the context of the claimant's social and cultural background."

paragraphs.summary: Appellant cites Giron advising caution on adverse findings from implausibilities due to cultural differences.

propositions.text: Claimant invokes IRPA 110(6) to be heard before RAD and call wife as witness.
propositions.quote: The claimant is invoking the provisions of subsection 110(6) of the IRPA, and is asking to be heard before the RAD and to call his wife as a witness.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant invokes IRPA 110(6) to be heard before RAD and call wife as witness.

propositions.text: Singh says RAD proceeds without hearing except where documentary evidence raises serious credibility issue central to decision and justifies allowing or rejecting claim.
propositions.quote: In Singh, the Federal Court of Appeal reiterated the principle that the RAD proceed without holding a hearing. According to the Court, this principle "is subject to an exception only where the documentary evidence '(a) [...] raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the person who is the subject of the appeal; (b) [...] is central to the decision with respect to the refugee protection claim; and (c) [...] if accepted, would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.'"

paragraphs.summary: Singh says RAD proceeds without hearing except where documentary evidence raises serious credibility issue central to decision and justifies allowing or rejecting claim.

propositions.text: Appellant submitted no new evidence; therefore RAD cannot hold a hearing.
propositions.quote: In this case, the appellant submitted no new evidence in support of his appeal. Therefore, the RAD cannot hold a hearing.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant submitted no new evidence; therefore RAD cannot hold a hearing.

propositions.text: Huruglica ruled on RAD's reasonableness standard when credibility not an issue for fact and law findings.
propositions.quote: In Huruglica, the Federal Court of Appeal ruled on the issue of whether it was reasonable for the RAD, when credibility was not an issue, to examine the findings of fact, mixed fact and law by using the reasonableness standard.

paragraphs.summary: Huruglica ruled on RAD's reasonableness standard when credibility not an issue for fact and law findings.

propositions.text: Justice Gauthier notes RAD was intended as safety net to catch RPD mistakes on law or facts.
propositions.quote: Interpreting the statutory provisions and making a passing reference to Parliament's intention in implementing the RAD, Justice Gauthier notes: [98] The RAD was essentially viewed as the safety net that would catch all mistakes made by the RPD, be it on the law or the facts.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Gauthier notes RAD was intended as safety net to catch RPD mistakes on law or facts.

propositions.text: Parliament intended IRPA ss 110 and 111 to allow RAD to correct RPD decisions wrong in law, fact or mixed fact and law, standard is correctness.
propositions.quote: Parliament's intention must be determined by referring first to the statute, specifically to sections 110 and 111 of the IRPA, about which the Court of Appeal indicates: [59] ... Paragraph 111(2)(a) does not distinguish between errors of law, fact or mixed fact and law. It simply requires that the decision of the RPD be "wrong in law, in fact or in mixed fact and law" (in French: "erronée en droit, en fait ou en droit et en fait"). [64] The ordinary meaning of the word "wrong" is "not correct or true", "incorrect", "mistaken": The Oxford English Dictionary, 3d ed., s.v. "wrong". The French version "erronée" has the exact same ordinary meaning, that is, "fausse", "incorrecte", "inexacte", "mal fondée": Le nouveau petit Robert, 2006, s.v. "erroné". This wording definitively points to the standard of correctness. In addition, the legislator's intent to use the word "wrong" in its ordinary meaning is, in my view, supported by the legislative history, to which I will refer later.

paragraphs.summary: Parliament intended IRPA ss 110 and 111 to allow RAD to correct RPD decisions wrong in law, fact or mixed fact and law, standard is correctness.

propositions.text: Legislative text recognizes RPD's advantage over RAD in findings involving credibility or weight of oral evidence.
propositions.quote: ... that there may be cases where the RPD enjoys a meaningful advantage over the RAD in making findings of fact or mixed fact and law, because they require an assessment of the credibility or weight to be given to the oral evidence it hears.

propositions.text: RAD should exercise restraint before substituting its own determination, assessed case-by-case.
propositions.quote: ... although the RAD should sometimes exercise a degree of restraint before substituting its own determination, the issue of whether the circumstances warrant such restraint ought to be addressed on a case-by-case basis.

propositions.text: RAD must determine if RPD had an advantageous position and if RAD can still make a final decision on the refugee claim.
propositions.quote: In each case, the RAD ought to determine whether the RPD truly benefited from an advantageous position, and if so, whether the RAD can nevertheless make a final decision in respect of the refugee claim.

paragraphs.summary: The Court states the legislative text recognizes RPD's advantage in credibility findings, RAD's restraint, and case-by-case assessment of RPD's advantage and RAD's final decision ability.

propositions.text: Level of deference owed by RAD varies; RAD intervenes if RPD is wrong in law, fact, or mixed fact and law applying correctness standard.
propositions.quote: At this stage of my analysis, I find that the role of the RAD is to intervene when the RPD is wrong in law, in fact or in fact and law. This translates into an application of the correctness standard of review.

propositions.text: If error found, RAD can confirm RPD decision on another basis or set it aside and substitute its own determination unless it cannot do so without hearing evidence.
propositions.quote: If there is an error, the RAD can still confirm the decision of the RPD on another basis. It can also set it aside, substituting its own determination of the claim, unless it is satisfied that it cannot do either without hearing the evidence presented to the RPD: paragraph 111(2)(b) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The Court of Appeal states RAD's deference varies; RAD applies correctness standard and can substitute decision unless it must hear evidence.

propositions.text: RAD reviews RPD findings of fact and mixed fact and law applying correctness standard when no credibility issue with oral evidence.
propositions.quote: ... with respect to findings of fact (and mixed fact and law) such as the one involved here, which raised no issue of credibility of oral evidence, the RAD is to review RPD decisions applying the correctness standard.

propositions.text: RAD must analyze record independently to confirm or set aside RPD decision and substitute its own determination if appropriate.
propositions.quote: ... the RAD carries out its own analysis of the record to determine whether, as submitted by the appellant, the RPD erred. Having done this, the RAD is to provide a final determination, either by confirming the RPD decision or setting it aside and substituting its own determination of the merits of the refugee claim.

propositions.text: RAD may refer matter back to RPD only if it cannot provide final determination without hearing oral evidence presented to RPD.
propositions.quote: It is only when the RAD is of the opinion that it cannot provide such a final determination without hearing the oral evidence presented to the RPD that the matter can be referred back to the RPD for redetermination.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Gauthier holds RAD applies correctness standard to RPD findings without credibility issues, independently analyzes record, and refers back only if oral evidence needed.

propositions.text: I will conduct independent analysis of evidence to determine correctness of refugee claim decision and intervene if error found.
propositions.quote: I will conduct an independent analysis of the evidence in order to formulate my own opinion on this refugee protection claim and to determine whether the decision rendered is correct. If an error of fact, of law or of mixed fact and law has been made, I will intervene through the remedies set out in the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court will independently analyze evidence and intervene if error of fact, law, or mixed fact and law is found.

propositions.text: Before RPD, the determinative issue was appellant's credibility.
propositions.quote: Before the RPD, the determinative issue was the appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: RPD has advantage over RAD in credibility assessments due to seeing and hearing claimants and witnesses.
propositions.quote: Generally, the RPD is in a more privileged position than the RAD because it has the advantage of seeing and hearing the refugee protection claimants and witnesses.

propositions.text: RAD will not have hearing privilege but must independently assess evidence to determine correctness and intervene if error found.
propositions.quote: In this case, the RAD will not have this privilege because it will not hold a hearing. However, I must conduct an independent assessment of the evidence to determine whether the decision rendered is correct. If an error of fact, of law or of mixed fact and law has been made, I will have to intervene through a method set out in the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD's determinative issue was credibility; RPD has hearing advantage, but RAD must independently assess evidence and intervene if error found.

propositions.text: I reviewed all evidence to form my opinion on refugee claim correctness.
propositions.quote: I reviewed all the evidence in order to formulate my own opinion on this refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Appellant's memorandum lacks eloquence on RPD errors in refugee claim assessment.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, I note that the appellant's memorandum is not very eloquent regarding the errors made by the RPD in the assessment of his refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: After considering arguments and evidence, I find RPD rendered correct decision.
propositions.quote: After considering the few arguments presented and the analysis of the evidence, it is my opinion that the RPD rendered the correct decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court reviewed evidence, found appellant's memorandum weak on errors, and concludes RPD decision was correct.

propositions.text: Presumption of truthfulness is rebuttable by claimant's lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: The presumption of truthfulness mentioned in Maldonado is not unchallengeable and a claimant's lack of credibility is sufficient to rebut it.

propositions.text: Accumulation of contradictions or omissions can justify negative credibility finding.
propositions.quote: although some evidence may not be sufficient when taken individually, the accumulation of contradictions or omissions may serve as a basis for a negative credibility finding

propositions.text: This case involves accumulation of contradictions or omissions undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: which is true in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The court states presumption of truthfulness is rebuttable by lack of credibility, including accumulated contradictions or omissions, as here.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's credibility undermined by omissions in BOC Form of key claim elements.
propositions.quote: One factor that the RPD found undermined the appellant's credibility was the omission in the BOC Form of several elements central to his refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Appellant testified threats from brother and cousin in 2015 for marrying Catholic and attending church, but did not mention in BOC Form.
propositions.quote: the appellant testified that, in XXXX 2015, his brother and his cousin had threatened to torture him because he had married a Catholic and was attending a Catholic church. However, the claimant did not mention these threats in his BOC Form.

propositions.text: RPD deemed appellant's explanation for omission insufficient.
propositions.quote: His explanation that he had put general information in his BOC Form without providing details was deemed insufficient by the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's credibility undermined by omissions in BOC Form about threats, and rejected his explanation for omission.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred in drawing negative inference from omission, claiming written form implied threats and fear.
propositions.quote: The appellant argued that the RPD erred in drawing a negative inference from that omission. He stated that he "testified in his written form that he feared his family, implying that they had threatened him and should not in any way undermine his credibility.

propositions.text: I cannot accept appellant's argument respecting omission and credibility.
propositions.quote: With due respect for the argument presented, I cannot accept it.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues RPD erred in negative inference from omission; the court rejects this argument.

propositions.text: Board can base negative credibility findings on omissions and inconsistencies in entry notes, Personal Information Form, and oral testimony.
propositions.quote: A long line of case law has established that the Board can base its negative credibility findings on the omissions and inconsistencies that it notes regarding the important facts alleged in the notes taken at the point of entry, in the Personal Information Form and in the oral testimony.

paragraphs.summary: Case law allows Board to base negative credibility findings on omissions and inconsistencies in various claimant statements.

propositions.text: RPD justified in drawing negative inference from claimant's failure to mention threats in BOC Form and provide details.
propositions.quote: The RPD was justified in drawing a negative inference from the fact that the claimant failed to mention those threats in the BOC Form and to give some details.

propositions.text: BOC Form question 2(a) requires detailed explanation of what happened and when.
propositions.quote: In fact, question 2(a) of the BOC Form requires claimants to explain in detail what happened to them and when.

propositions.text: Claimant also failed to indicate cousin's toughness and membership in a Tunisian group in BOC Form, which relate to threats.
propositions.quote: Likewise, the appellant failed to indicate in the BOC Form that his cousin is a tough man, that he is a member of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX an XXXXgroupXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in Tunisia.

propositions.text: RPD noted these facts are not trivial as they relate to basis of fear.
propositions.quote: As the RPD noted, these are not trivial facts; they relate to the threats that form the basis of his fear.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD was justified in negative inference from omissions in BOC Form about threats and related facts, which are not trivial.

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from claimant's failure to indicate family marginalization in BOC Form despite testifying about it.
propositions.quote: The RPD drew a negative inference from the fact that the claimant also failed to indicate in the BOC Form that his family marginalized him in Tunisia because he did not follow the precepts of Islam; he drank alcohol, did not go to the mosque regularly and did not observe Ramadan in XXXX.

propositions.text: Omission undermined credibility especially since claimant stated no religious problems in BOC Form.
propositions.quote: The omission of these aspects in the BOC Form, about which he testified, undermined his credibility, especially since the claimant stated in the BOC Form that he did not have any problems in Tunisia due to his religion.

paragraphs.summary: RPD negatively inferred from claimant's omission of family marginalization in BOC Form, undermining credibility.

propositions.text: RPD noted important contradiction: claimant said in BOC Form he attended church with wife but testified he went without her.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted a contradiction that I find important. The claimant stated in the BOC Form that he attended XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX church with his wife. Yet, at the hearing, he stated that he went without her.

propositions.text: This contradiction is not trivial and supports serious doubt about claimant's church attendance.
propositions.quote: This is not a trivial contradiction and tends to support serious doubt when he states he attends a Christian church.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found a significant contradiction about church attendance with wife, supporting serious doubt; the court agrees.

propositions.text: Claimant contradicted himself about frequency and language of mass attendance.
propositions.quote: The appellant also contradicted himself about how frequently he attended mass and the language in which it was celebrated.

propositions.text: Initially said attended mass 4-5 times on XXXX XXXX in XXXX; changed to attending two churches after confrontation.
propositions.quote: At the hearing, he stated first that he attended mass four or five times on XXXX XXXXnd that the mass was in XXXX. When confronted with the fact that mass at the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is on XXXX and that it is celebrated in XXXX and in XXXX, the claimant changed his testimony and answered that he attended two churches.

propositions.text: These contradictions are not trivial and support serious doubt about claimant's church attendance.
propositions.quote: Again, the facts are not trivial; his attending a Christian church is at the heart of his problems. The contradictions in his testimony tend to support serious doubt.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant contradicted himself on mass attendance frequency and language; these contradictions support serious doubt.

propositions.text: RPD found claimant did not convert to Catholicism or intend to, considering lack of catechism classes and inability to name sacraments.
propositions.quote: In the credibility assessment, and to find that "the panel believes that the claimant did not convert to Catholicism and did not demonstrate that he intended to do so," the RPD also considered the following factors. The claimant did not take catechism classes and did not register for catechism classes. He is unable to name one of the sacraments of the Catholic religion.

propositions.text: Claimant claimed to have consulted parish priest about baptism but did not know priest's name.
propositions.quote: This may seem unimportant, but in this case, the appellant claims to have consulted the parish priest about a possible baptism and, furthermore, he did not know the name of the priest with whom he had discussed this.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found claimant did not convert or intend to, noting lack of catechism classes and ignorance of priest's name despite baptism claim.

propositions.text: Testimony cannot be discredited solely for lack of corroboration but absence of expected corroboration may be considered.
propositions.quote: A claimant's testimony cannot be discredited simply because it is not corroborated by the documentary evidence. However, the Board may take account of the absence of corroborative evidence in circumstances where one would expect it to exist.

propositions.text: RPD had serious doubts about claimant's allegations due to accumulation of problems.
propositions.quote: In this case, the RPD, due to an accumulation of problems related to the claimant's statements, had serious doubts about his allegations.

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from appellant's wife not corroborating testimony by affidavit or testimony.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, it was justified in this context to draw a negative inference from the fact that the appellant's wife did not corroborate the claimant's testimony either by testifying directly or by submitting an affidavit.

propositions.text: RPD noted appellant's lack of effort to obtain wife's affidavit undermined credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that the appellant's lack of effort to obtain an affidavit from his wife undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: I agree RPD was justified to consider lack of wife's corroboration as undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: In my opinion, it was an element that the RPD could have expected and, in the context of this case, the RPD was justified to consider that element.

paragraphs.summary: Testimony alone is not discredited by lack of corroboration, but RPD reasonably drew negative inference from wife's absence of corroboration and appellant's lack of effort.

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from implausibility that conservative Catholic family allowed daughter to marry Muslim man before conversion.
propositions.quote: The RPD drew a negative inference from the implausibility that a conservative Catholic family had allowed their daughter to marry a Muslim man before he converted, when it was a condition of their accepting the union.

paragraphs.summary: RPD negatively inferred from implausibility of conservative Catholic family allowing daughter to marry Muslim man before conversion.

propositions.text: Credibility findings based on implausibility require clearest cases, unlike those based on inconsistencies or contradictions.
propositions.quote: In Subramaniyathas, the Federal Court states: "In contrast to credibility findings based on inconsistencies, contradictions or evasions, credibility findings based on implausibility may only be made in the clearest of cases."

propositions.text: I consider implausibility finding not determinative in this case.
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that this finding is not determinative in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes implausibility findings require clearest cases and finds it not determinative here.

propositions.text: RPD found it curious claimant renounced Islam but still presents as Muslim.
propositions.quote: As noted by the RPD, it is curious that the refugee protection claimant stated that he had renounced Islam but that he still presents himself as Muslim.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found it curious claimant renounced Islam but still presents as Muslim.

propositions.text: I conclude RPD rendered correct decision; appellant did not show decision was unsupported or erroneous in fact, law, or mixed fact and law.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, it is my opinion that the RPD rendered the correct decision in this case; the appellant did not establish that the decision is not based on the evidence or that the RPD committed an error in fact, in law or in mixed fact and law.

propositions.text: Based on evidence, I would have rendered the same decision.
propositions.quote: In light of the evidence in the record, I would have rendered the same decision.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the RPD decision was correct and it would have reached the same conclusion based on evidence.

propositions.text: Confirm the RPD's determination that XXXX XXXX is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97
propositions.quote: I confirm the determination of the RPD, namely, that XXXX XXXX is neither a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA nor a "person in need of protection" under section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the RPD's determination that XXXX XXXX is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: Dismiss the appeal
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal.
